headline: Gas shortage deepens Bangladesh power crisis, load-shedding hits 3,592MW
summary: Bangladesh is grappling with severe gas shortages, leading to extensive power outages across the country. Citizens face long queues at CNG stations and unlit stoves at home, highlighting the widespread impact of the energy crisis.
details: Bangladesh is currently experiencing a severe energy crisis, with gas shortages leading to widespread power outages. Load-shedding across the country has reached an alarming 3,592 megawatts, significantly impacting daily life and industrial operations.

The scarcity of natural gas has crippled power generation, as many power plants rely heavily on gas as fuel. This has resulted in frequent and prolonged electricity cuts, disrupting businesses, education, and household activities.

Beyond electricity, the gas shortage is also affecting domestic consumers and the transport sector. Households are reporting unlit stoves, making cooking difficult, while long queues are observed at CNG refueling stations.

Experts attribute the crisis to Bangladesh's increasing reliance on imported fuel and the volatile global energy market. The current situation underscores the vulnerability of an import-dependent energy sector to international price fluctuations and supply disruptions.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh pacers reduce Australia to 74/4]] at lunch on Day 1 of Darwin Test
headline: Bangladesh pacers reduce Australia to 74/4 at lunch on Day 1 of Darwin Test
summary: Hasan Mahmud struck twice, while Ebadot Hossain and Taskin Ahmed each claimed a wicket, leaving Australia struggling at 74 for four by lunch in the opening Test in Darwin.
details: Bangladesh pacers Hasan Mahmud, Ebadot Hossain, and Taskin Ahmed made early inroads, reducing Australia to 74 for four at lunch on Day 1 of the first Test in Darwin. Hasan Mahmud led the attack with two crucial wickets, setting the tone for the visitors.

After a cautious start by Australia's openers, Hasan Mahmud struck twice in successive overs. He removed Jake Weatherald (23) in the 12th over and Travis Head (22) in the 14th over, breaking their initial partnership.

Ebadot Hossain then joined the wicket-taking spree, dismissing Marnus Labuschagne for just one run in the 19th over. This further dented Australia's top order, leaving them under significant pressure.

Taskin Ahmed capped off an excellent opening session by removing Cameron Green for 13 at the stroke of lunch. This brought Bangladesh's total wickets to four, showcasing a dominant bowling performance.

In the second session, Ebadot provided another breakthrough, bowling Alex Carey for 19 and ending a 56-run partnership with Steve Smith. Taskin then struck again, bowling Beau Webster for 12, leaving Australia at 152 for six.

Steve Smith remained unbeaten on 50, his 45th Test half-century, attempting to stabilize the innings amidst the Bangladeshi onslaught. Australia reached 157 for six after 40 overs when the report was filed.
caption:
